coverageContext: Complete 68-variant QT-interval research score using original QT GWAS beta coefficients. GA reports the genetic sum, not measured or predicted ECG milliseconds or the study-standardized score. European evaluation included 1238 LQTS cases and 8219 controls; 1115 cases carried a rare major-gene variant and only 123 were genotype negative. Japanese analyses used 60/68 variants plus a proxy, so their results and combined-ancestry results do not validate this exact full 68-term definition. Catalog ancestry summaries retain those study records but must not imply full-model transferability. This is a cardiac electrophysiology research trait, not a long-QT diagnosis, absolute disease probability, cardiac-event prediction, medication-safety test or substitute for an ECG or clinical rare-variant assessment.
